articles.headline: Inside George Kittle's 243-day recovery from torn Achilles
articles.description: Despite tearing his Achilles in the playoffs, Kittle appears to be back to his normal self. Here's how he won the recovery process.
articles.body:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. -- At 5:30 on a late March morning, eight weeks after surgery to repair his torn right Achilles, San Francisco 49ers tight end George Kittle was wide-awake.

Kittle and a close group of friends had traveled to Bandon Dunes Golf Resort in Oregon for six rounds in four days. For 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk and others of the traveling party, it was a leisurely weekend on the links. For Kittle, it was an important step in his road back to the football field, a path he had defiantly proclaimed could have him ready for Week 1 in Melbourne, Australia. Which is why, when Juszczyk came downstairs to begin loosening up for that day's rounds, he found Kittle meticulously picking up a towel with his toes.

It was a prime example of Kittle's disciplined approach to rehab his injured Achilles, and a side of Kittle the public rarely sees beneath the ebullient pro wrestling persona. This was the passionate, football-obsessed Kittle who had no desire to let anyone else author the timeline of his return.

"It's fun to be doubted," Kittle, 32, told ESPN last week. "I'm not a chip-on-my-shoulder guy whatsoever, but when you have all the people who are like, 'Oh, you're not doing this, you're not doing that.' I'm like, 'I am doing that and extra. You believe whatever you want, you can talk however you want to talk, but when you see me Week 1, you can kick rocks.'"

Kittle's discipline fueled an odds-defying, 243-day recovery from a torn Achilles suffered in a Jan. 11 NFC wild-card win over the Philadelphia Eagles. Through those eight months, he channeled his usual golden retriever energy into tedious daily rehab.

The usual recovery can take anywhere from eight months to a year, and a June 2026 study done at Michigan State University and published in the Physician and Sportsmedicine Journal said only 27.1% of NFL players return to pre-injury performance levels. But so far this season, Kittle has reasserted himself as one of the league's best tight ends. After knocking off rust in the opener against the Rams, Kittle has posted 10 receptions for 162 yards and three touchdowns in the past two weeks -- second-most receiving yards among all tight ends over that span.

Kittle's recovery required shuttling between physical therapists in Los Angeles (Heather Milligan) and Nashville (Jorge Rojas, DPT), as well as check-ins with the 49ers. With the guidance of Dr. Neil ElAttrache, the Los Angeles-based surgeon who performed the Achilles repair on Jan. 14, Kittle's team devised a blueprint to make his Week 1 dream a reality. Executing that plan was up to him.

"As an athlete, you have to have that special sauce that you're really willing to push yourself to the very limit so that you can get back," Milligan said. "You don't wish injury on anybody, but the matchup of what it takes on this rehab with his personality and focus is a huge part of why he was so successful.

"You've got the best patient in the world."

articles.headline: Hard to see how Man City recover from extraordinary guilty verdict
articles.description: Tuesday's confirmation that Manchester City were found guilty by the Premier League on over 100 breaches of financial regulations has sent shockwaves through the sport. How do Man City survive this?
articles.body:
And now it's official: according to the Premier League's three-person independent commission, Manchester City have been found guilty of inflated revenues and lowered costs through "sham" (the league's own remark) sponsorship deals, self-dealing image rights contracts with phony companies and off-the-books payments.

This inflated reporting enabled them to disguise more than £900 million ($1.18 billion) as legitimate commercial revenue over a nine-year period when, in fact, it was nothing more than the owner, Abu Dhabi United Group (ADUG), dipping into the family coffers. In so doing, they severely breached the Financial Sustainability rules laid out by the Premier League and UEFA -- regulations they publicly endorsed and claimed to support. Along the way, among the 100+ charges they were also found guilty of false accounting -- which is somewhat inevitable when you misstate the source and scope of your income -- failing to cooperate with investigators and failing to "act in the utmost good faith." All in all, a breathtaking set of findings.

After Friday's news that City had been found guilty had broken, but was not yet official, City chairman Khaldoon Al-Mubarak issued a statement Saturday saying "our confidence and intent in proving the club's innocence is just as strong as when this began." He also made reference to "irrefutable evidence," which felt odd when he knew it had been refuted just 48 hours earlier by the independent commission. City are entitled to appeal the decision by this Friday, though it's worth noting that no new evidence can be brought in as part of the appeal process.

- Dawson: Man City's guilt the talk of the town in English soccer

- Premier League findings: Scope and scale of Man City's wrongdoing

- Sources: Man City learned of guilty verdicts before busy summer transfers

We are not privy to the entire judgement -- partly because it's freakishly long and dense, partly due to the Premier League's confidentiality rules -- but the 40-page "Core Decision," even with its myriad redactions, illustrates quite clearly the case against City and doesn't pull punches in terms of its language, describing City's actions as a "sham" on several occasions.

For those who have followed the case over the past 15 years, covered the settlement agreement with UEFA in 2014 when City were first punished for breaching Financial Fair Play rules (an agreement brokered by one Gianni Infantino in an earlier life) and covered the subsequent UEFA ban in February 2020 and City's successful appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) that same summer, not much of this is new. Most of it was there in Der Spiegel's investigation into the Football Leaks documents in 2018, and it was those revelations that prompted the Premier League's investigation.

Sept. 29

Charania: NBA reviewing finalists' bids for Vegas team

ESPN's Shams Charania reported that the NBA is currently reviewing finalist bids for a new expansion team in Las Vegas. The price range is currently speculated at $12-13 billion with a new arena factored into the cost. 

The three final groups are Nancy Walton Laurie and Bill Laurie; Steve Apostolopoulos and Marc Lasry; Bill Foley and Jerry Colangelo, sources told ESPN.

Embiid "full participant" in first Sixers' practice

Joel Embiid was a "full participant all the way through" for the Philadelphia 76ers first practice of training camp, Sixers coach Nick Nurse said Tuesday.

"He looked great," Nurse said of Embiid. "Very, very good news from the standpoint of where it's been the last couple years, last couple summers leading into today. ... It's great to see."

After being named the league MVP in 2023, the 32-year-old center has missed 150 games over the last three seasons because of various injuries.

He also sat out four of the Sixers' 11 playoff games in the spring because of appendicitis, right hip soreness and a right ankle sprain.

The only Sixers player who did not participate in Tuesday's practice according to a team spokesperson was backup big man Adem Bona, who is dealing with a sprained left foot.

Anfernee Simons, who signed a two-year, $12.3 million contract to join Philadelphia in July, said Embiid's presence in the gym was already notable leading up to the start of camp.

"Everybody's been impressed around here about how he's come in and worked," Simons said. "Joel is going to be Joel. He's going to be a dominant player always. We just want to continue for him to be himself, as well, and I think everybody's going to be able to work around that."

Despite the injuries, the 10-year veteran still averaged 26.9 points, 7.7 rebounds, 3.9 assists and 1.2 blocks per game last season.

Embiid's inclusion only added to what several Sixers players described as an "exciting" opening day with LeBron James and Jaylen Brown completing their first official practice with the franchise.

articles.headline: Sources: NBA reviewing bids from three finalists for Vegas team
articles.description: The NBA is expected to select the winning bid for owner of the Vegas expansion team from among three finalist group: Nancy Walton Laurie and Bill Laurie; Steve Apostolopoulos and Marc Lasry; Bill Foley and Jerry Colangelo.
articles.body:
The NBA is expected to select the winning bid for owner of the Las Vegas expansion team in the very near future, with a price of at least $12-13 billion for the franchise and new arena among three finalist groups -- Nancy Walton Laurie and Bill Laurie; Steve Apostolopoulos and Marc Lasry; Bill Foley and Jerry Colangelo, sources told ESPN.

The league, which will hold a formal approval process by the end of December on two expansion teams, is closing on Las Vegas before Seattle for several reasons. Las Vegas has a livelier bidding market with higher offers and the process consists of the logistics of developing a new arena versus Climate Pledge Arena already being a ready-made home for the Seattle team. The Vegas runners-up also could potentially join the Seattle bid process.

Nancy Walton Laurie is the daughter of Walmart co-founder James "Bud" Walton. Her husband, Bill Laurie, is a former owner of the NHL's St. Louis Blues. The two have a home in Henderson, Nevada, a suburb of Las Vegas, and they have a net worth of $17 billion, according to Forbes.

 

Apostolopoulos, a Canadian billionaire, discussed buying the Charlotte Hornets from Michael Jordan in 2023 but instead focused on purchasing the NFL's Washington Commanders. That franchise was later sold for $6.05 billion to a group led by Josh Harris, who also owns the Philadelphia 76ers and the NHL's New Jersey Devils. Apostolopoulos, 46, has a known desire to build a wide-ranging portfolio across multiple sports leagues.

Apostolopoulos and his brothers, Jim and Peter Apostolopoulos, lead the group with Lasry as a partner.

Lasry is the former co-owner of the Milwaukee Bucks. In 2023, he sold his stake to Cleveland Browns owners Jimmy and Dee Haslam at a valuation of $3.5 billion.

Colangelo, the former owner of the Phoenix Suns, said in July that he was entering the bidding with his Las Vegas Jacks group. His announcement came one month after Foley, the majority owner of the NHL's Vegas Golden Knights, said he wanted to bring an NBA team to the city.

Colangelo's group and Foley began talking about joining forces four months ago, and have agreed to partner because of Foley's ties to the city combined with the Jacks' plans for a new arena and the group's relationship equity with key league stakeholders. Foley said in June that his potential NBA franchise would play at T-Mobile Arena, where his Golden Knights have games, but sources said a new arena will be built if the Colangelo-Foley group wins the bid.

The Jacks group includes former Turner Sports president David Levy and Scott Colangelo, a managing partner at Prime Capital Financial. Former NBA player and coach Vinny Del Negro and ESPN basketball analyst Jay Williams are members too.

Colangelo, a Hall of Famer, sold the Suns in 2004 for a then-record $401 million. He's a four-time NBA executive of the year, and he was managing director of USA Basketball from 2005 to 2021, guiding the program to four Olympic gold medals. Colangelo has serv

articles.headline: Man City CEO says Premier League verdict part of 'conspiracy'
articles.description: Manchester City chief executive officer Ferran Soriano has claimed the bombshell guilty verdict against the club is the result of a "Premier League conspiracy theory."
articles.body:
Manchester City chief executive officer Ferran Soriano has claimed the bombshell guilty verdict against the club is the result of a "Premier League conspiracy theory" and that the club will appeal the ruling.

City were found guilty on Tuesday of all charges related to breaches of Premier League financial rules between 2009-10 and 2017-18 by an independent commission.

The club said they will appeal "on the basis that the opinion contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe."

In a video message to club staff, Soriano said: "A document has been made public with an opinion of the Premier League commission which is negative to our interests.

"I want to explain exactly what this is, the next steps, and how we are going to continue to defend the club and finally be vindicated in this process.

"This has gone on for so long that it's important to remind ourselves that the whole Premier League case against us is based on a single false accusation; that the owner's personal money was somehow and secretly put into the club via some sponsors from Abu Dhabi.

"This is just not true. Irrefutable evidence has been provided to the Premier League commission that shows that it could not happen and that it did not happen.

"This includes bank statements, money transfers, witnesses, and everything necessary to categorically demonstrate the money did not come from the owner.

"Every other false charge that has been thrown at us and aggressively marketed and promoted comes from that simple, central, and completely false accusation.

"Surprisingly for us and for our lawyers, after nearly two years, the Premier League commission has issued an opinion that supports the Premier League's conspiracy theory.

"To do so, the opinion had to actually ignore the extensive evidence provided by the club in order to reach a conclusion that is clearly wrong.

"Our lawyers will now file an appeal that sets out that the opinion contains clear material errors of law, principle, and fact, and it is unsafe."

In 2020 City successfully overturned a two-year ban from European club competitions, imposed by UEFA for breaching Financial Fair Play regulations, after taking the case to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS).

"Remember, we have been here before," added Soriano. "In 2020, we were also wrongly ruled against for many of the same issues. We appealed to an independent body, CAS, and we won.

"We will now be relentless in our work. We will focus on the independent appeal process and also all other legal avenues available to us in order to win the case.

"And we will take all necessary action to protect the club and seek compensation from any party that tries to damage it, now and in the future.

"I know this can be a bit of a distraction, but please remain focused on our business and taking care of our extended City family, as we always do.

Internazionale are eyeing a January move for United States and Crystal Palace defender Chris Richards, while Real Madrid midfielder Aurélien Tchouaméni is still on the radar of Liverpool. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Trending rumors

- Internazionale are eyeing a January move for USMNT and Crystal Palace defender Chris Richards, according to Tuttosport. Inter scouts have been tracking the 26-year-old, who operates on the right side of Palace's back three, as part of the club's plan to bring in free agents. Richards' contract expires in 2027 and he could bolster a defense already containing new arrivals Djed Spence and John Stones.

- Liverpool have maintained contact with the representatives of Real Madrid midfielder Aurélien Tchouaméni despite the 26-year-old signing a new deal until 2031, according to TEAMtalk. While the Reds are not actively pursuing the France international right now, they could revive their interest if his role under José Mourinho changes given he has only played three times so far this season. Madrid had reportedly been willing to listen to offers of around €80 million over the summer.

- Manchester City will refuse to allow striker Erling Haaland to leave on the cheap even if they face relegation as a result of their legal battle with the Premier League, reports Football Insider. Arsenal, Real Madrid and Barcelona are paying close attention to the 26-year-old's situation, but City hold a strong negotiating position as his contract runs until 2034 with no relegation release clause.

- Chelsea remain interested in signing Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara in January despite his €55 million deadline-day transfer collapsing, according to TEAMtalk. Liverpool, Crystal Palace, Brighton & Hove Albion and Newcastle United are also tracking the 22-year-old Senegal international, who is keen on a January switch, though Monaco's willingness to sanction his exit remains uncertain.

- Beşiktaş president Serdal Adalı has vowed to sign Newcastle United midfielder Joe Willock in January, as per TalkSPORT. The 27-year-old is in the final year of his contract and can agree to a pre-contract with overseas clubs in January, though he has featured regularly under new boss Matthias Jaissle this season.

articles.headline: Knockout league pickups: Josh Allen, Justin Jefferson among big names available in Week 4
articles.description: Tristan H. Cockcroft lists the most common players on eliminated teams and finds how much FAB to spend this week.
articles.body:
If the 2026 NFL season is reiterating any key lesson, it's this: Anything goes.

The Las Vegas Raiders, 150-1 (0.66% implied odds) to win the Super Bowl at the onset of the season, are 3-0 with an 11.3-point average victory margin. Conversely, the Houston Texans, 18-1 (5.3%) entering Week 1, have dropped three in a row with their vaunted defense having surrendered the 14th-most points (25.0 per game).

In fantasy football, Brock Purdy, a 10th-round pick on average during the preseason, is the No. 4 overall scorer, averaging only 4.3 fewer fantasy points per game than Josh Allen. Meanwhile, Omarion Hampton, a popular breakout pick and the No. 15 overall player in terms of ADP, has averaged 10.5 points to place outside the top 20 in scoring among running backs.

That "any given Sunday" aspect to the NFL, and fantasy football, certainly took hold in Knockout leagues in Week 3. After each of the first two weeks saw three players reside on at least 15% of teams knocked out, not one reached that threshold this past weekend. This was also the first week in which a player exceeded 10 fantasy points yet appeared on a knocked out team in 10% or more of leagues, both of them quarterbacks: Allen (17.46 points, 10.4% knocked out) and Jalen Hurts (12.62, 10.1%).

Poor quarterback play continues to influence Knockout results. Besides Allen's and Hurts' performances, Drake Maye, who has yet to score as many as 10 fantasy points in a game, is one of four players (A.J. Brown, Kenny Gainwell and Kyle Pitts Sr. are the others) to place on at least 8% of teams knocked out in the first three weeks. Justin Herbert has averaged 11.3 fantasy points and ranks 26th in total points scored at the position, getting his teams bumped from Knockout play in 9.2% of leagues in Week 2 and 7.2% this past week. Injuries to Jayden Daniels (10.6%), Caleb Williams (8.0%) and Baker Mayfield (5.9%) also proved costly to Knockout managers this week.

Quarterback strategy can prove critical in Knockout play, and with this being the first week in which we've seen a multi-year star make it to free agency, investment time at the position might be here (or certainly arriving if you're not in a league where one of those prominent names is available for the taking). Let's dive right in.

articles.headline: Knicks still undecided if they will visit White House
articles.description: The Knicks are still deciding if they will become the first NBA champions to visit the White House under President Donald Trump.
articles.body:
GREENBURGH, N.Y. -- The New York Knicks are still deciding whether they will become the first NBA champions to visit the White House under President Donald Trump, coach Mike Brown said Tuesday.

The president has traditionally invited the reigning champions, but that has not been the case under Trump. No team went during his first term or after he was elected again in 2024.

But Trump and Knicks owner James Dolan are close. They sat together when Trump attended Game 3 of the NBA Finals at Madison Square Garden, and Dolan indicated after the Knicks won the championship that an offer would be accepted.

The Knicks held their first practice of the new season Tuesday and Brown was asked if there was a determination about a White House visit.

"No, it's still something that our guys, or the organization, is internally discussing and, you know, whatever we decide to do, we'll all do together," Brown said.

The Boston Celtics made the first trip by a champion in 1963, and President Barack Obama, who is a basketball fan, hosted the winner every year he was in office.

But Trump has feuded with some NBA players, saying during the 2018 NBA Finals that he wouldn't invite whichever team won, after Golden State's Stephen Curry and LeBron James, then with the Cleveland Cavaliers, said their teams had no interest in a visit.

The 2025 champion Oklahoma City Thunder didn't visit the White House last season, saying the timing did not work out.

Teams often try to arrange their visit when they are in Washington to play the Wizards. The Knicks are scheduled for those games on Dec. 18 and March 16.
